A 16-bit SNES-style PIXEL ART character WALK sheet on a SOLID FLAT PURE WHITE background (#FFFFFF, completely uniform). Layout: 3 ROWS by 3 COLUMNS of sprites, evenly spaced, with a wide empty white margin on all four sides and a clear white gap between every sprite — nothing may touch, overlap or be cut off by any edge, especially the bottom row. Every sprite is the SAME character at the SAME size and the SAME pixel scale. THE CHARACTER, drawn identically in all nine frames: {CHARACTER}. THE THREE COLUMNS are the walk cycle, left to right: Column 1 = MID-STEP with her LEFT foot planted forward and her right foot back, a clear gap between the feet, arms swinging. Column 2 = NEUTRAL STANDING — both legs straight and together directly under the body, arms hanging relaxed, no stride, no lean, no leaning weapon pose. This is the standing-still pose and it must be obviously different from columns 1 and 3. Column 3 = MID-STEP with her RIGHT foot planted forward and her left foot back — the opposite stride to column 1, and clearly NOT a repeat of the standing pose in column 2. THE THREE ROWS are directions, and the direction must hold across ALL THREE frames of its row without exception — including the neutral standing frame: Row 1 = seen from the FRONT, facing the viewer. Row 2 = strict SIDE PROFILE FACING RIGHT — head in profile, nose pointing right, one shoulder to the viewer, in all three frames INCLUDING the neutral standing one; never turned to face the viewer. Row 3 = seen from BEHIND — the back of the head and body, NO face, NO eyes, NO snout. ART STYLE: chunky flat cartoon pixel art, big simple shapes, flat solid colours, a thick black outline, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no dithering, no texture inside a colour block. Nothing else in the image: no grid lines, no boxes, no frames, no labels, no text, no numbers, no shadows.
